headline: Lyall Atkinson launches mayoral campaign site
summary: Atkinson’s campaign site frames his mayoral run around financial accountability, transparency, fair process, downtown recovery, public safety, taxpayer protection and better consultation.

headline: Mike Harris campaign site sets out mayoral priorities
summary: Harris’s campaign site describes a mayoral platform focused on public safety, taxpayer value, housing permit timelines, downtown conditions, neighbourhood listening and an independent review of City Hall.

headline: Elections BC posts registered-candidates finance snapshot
summary: Elections BC published a registered-candidates finance snapshot that includes 14 Victoria mayoral and council records. This is a campaign-finance registration source, not the complete City nomination roster, so the City declaration remains the authority for who is officially declared.

headline: Livable CRD publishes Victoria candidate questionnaire snapshot
summary: The current Livable CRD Victoria scorecard says six candidates returned its questionnaire: Mike Harris, Jeremy Caradonna, Matt Dell, Martin Girard, Bella Lee and Jack Sandor. Individual pages for Bella Lee and Jack Sandor still show no reply, so this is recorded as third-party questionnaire coverage rather than an endorsement or settled response status.

headline: Victoria all-candidate forum on food systems announced for October 5
summary: Victoria Urban Food Table lists an in-person all-candidate forum for October 5, 2026, at Fernwood Community Centre. The listing does not name participating candidates, so no attendance is inferred.

headline: City declares candidates for Victoria mayor and council
summary: The City announced that the Declaration of Candidates for the 2026 local government election is available. The declaration lists eight mayoral candidates and 21 council candidates for the City of Victoria race.

headline: CivicInfo posts Victoria candidate list and online campaign links
summary: CivicInfo BC published a Victoria candidate page sourced from local election officials, including candidate names, previous-office status, and contact or online campaign links where candidates consented to display them.

headline: Victoria firefighters union prepares candidate-endorsement campaign
summary: Victoria Buzz reports that IAFF Local 730 will engage in the municipal election as a third-party advertising sponsor and ask candidates to respond to priorities on emergency response, single-stair egress, violence against first responders and mental-health support.

headline: My re-election platform – your ideas are welcome, as always
summary: Dave Thompson says his developing re-election platform reflects feedback from residents and business owners. Preliminary priorities include housing variety, homelessness and mental-health supports, safer streets, climate action and trees, a vibrant local economy, and responsible, evidence-based governance.

headline: A Practical Plan to Restore Public Safety
summary: Jerry Garcia outlined a public-safety plan combining visible safety resources, focused enforcement, cleaner public spaces, coordinated responses, access to treatment and supportive housing, business support, prevention, and public performance reporting.

headline: Mike Harris for mayor??? God help us!!!
summary: Martin Girard published political commentary criticizing mayoral candidate Mike Harris. The entry is labelled opinion and does not treat its allegations as independently verified facts.

headline: Stories from Pandora Avenue
summary: Martin Girard published first-person accounts about unhoused residents on Pandora Avenue and argued that enforcement and displacement do not resolve homelessness. This is candidate commentary.

headline: My 10-point plan to relieve the pressure on Pandora Avenue
summary: Martin Girard published a ten-point proposal for Pandora Avenue that emphasizes outreach, shelter and washroom access, supportive services, alternatives to displacement, and renewed attention to the needs of unhoused residents.

headline: Reconciliation Through Respect, Partnership, and Results
summary: Jerry Garcia published a reconciliation proposal focused on government-to-government relationships with the Songhees and Xwsepsum Nations, Indigenous economic participation, cooperation on shared regional challenges, and public reporting of commitments and results.

headline: Protecting and Growing Victoria’s Urban Forest
summary: Jerry Garcia proposed protecting mature trees while continuing to build housing, planting in lower-canopy areas, coordinating tree planning with streets and utilities, and publicly measuring canopy outcomes.

headline: Victoria noise rules, transit strike talks, ferry fairness and Saanich Fair
summary: Marianne Alto discussed the City’s planned noise-bylaw rewrite, including construction-noise hours and the possibility of phasing out leaf blowers, alongside regional transportation and ferry issues.

headline: Martin Girard shares a personal campaign biography
summary: Martin Girard published a personal biography describing disability, former homelessness, advocacy work, legal self-representation and his reasons for seeking a seat on Victoria council.

headline: Times Colonist letter: Charter of Rights should not be bypassed
summary: Martin Girard published a candidate-authored response arguing that Charter protections should not be bypassed in addressing homelessness. This is recorded as candidate commentary, not independent reporting.

headline: Bruce McGuigan publishes mayoral campaign priorities
summary: McGuigan's candidate-owned site confirms his mayoral campaign and sets out positions on homelessness, housing, public safety, accountable government, local economic development, climate resilience and the arts. The page did not expose a publication date.

headline: Victoria mayor and council candidates make their cases as nominations open
summary: CTV reports detailed campaign priorities from Marianne Alto, Bruce McGuigan and eight council candidates, covering housing, homelessness, safety, taxes, public accountability, climate resilience, regional services, transportation and the downtown economy.

headline: Nomination period opens for Victoria Election 2026
summary: The City says nomination packages may be filed from September 1 at 9 a.m. until September 11 at 4 p.m. No Victoria mayoral or council filings appeared in the official sources checked for this update.

headline: City posts 2026 election and nomination information
summary: The City's current election page confirms October 17 as general voting day, with nominations accepted September 1–11. No nomination filing or final ballot notice was available at retrieval time.

headline: Krista Loughton launches Team Loughton 2026 site
summary: Loughton's campaign site asks voters to re-elect her and describes a supportive-housing transition proposal and a walkable 'City of Communities' approach. The page did not expose a publication date.

headline: Marg Gardiner sets out re-election platform
summary: Gardiner's undated campaign site presents positions on policing, treatment, neighbourhood planning, zero-based budgeting and public consultation. The item date reflects retrieval, not original publication.

headline: Martin Girard publishes council campaign platform
summary: Girard's undated campaign site states positions on municipal drug policy, Indigenous rights and selected international human-rights issues. The item date reflects retrieval, not original publication.

headline: Shona Dion publishes council campaign priorities
summary: Dion's undated campaign page outlines positions on social and co-operative housing, climate adaptation, bicycle infrastructure, public ownership and worker safety. The item date reflects retrieval, not original publication.

headline: Dave Thompson says he will seek re-election
summary: Thompson's refreshed campaign site says he is running again for council. It identifies housing, safer streets, vulnerable residents and climate as developing priorities.

headline: Victoria For All launches council candidates Susan Kim and Peter Rose Gibbs
summary: The report covers an August 15 launch naming Kim and Rose Gibbs as Victoria council candidates. It summarizes the group's shared focus on community care, housing, climate and accessible public spaces; its school-board candidate is outside this monitor's scope.

headline: Jerry Garcia announces Victoria council campaign
summary: Garcia's campaign announcement identifies economic growth, public safety, homelessness and fiscal responsibility as priorities for a council bid.

headline: Stephen Hammond opens re-election campaign
summary: Hammond's campaign site confirms a council re-election bid and highlights public safety, affordable taxation, practical housing measures and renter protection.

headline: Bella Lee and Jack Sandor launch council campaigns focused on housing
summary: The report introduces Lee and Sandor as council candidates and describes their shared emphasis on housing costs, public services and a city where younger residents can remain.

headline: Arthur McInnis publishes Victoria council platform
summary: McInnis's campaign presents governance, budget, housing, transportation and safety proposals, including an integrity commissioner and zero-based budgeting.

headline: Municipal Courage with Victoria Mayor Marianne Alto
summary: In an interview, Marianne Alto discussed housing pressure, homelessness, mental health and addiction, shelter and transitional-housing spaces, the City’s Community Safety and Wellbeing department, and municipal support for nonprofit services.

headline: Karen Rothe launches campaign for Victoria council
summary: Rothe's campaign emphasizes transparent government, downtown renewal, proactive planning and attention to municipal core services.

headline: Victoria Mayor Marianne Alto launches re-election campaign
summary: The report confirms Alto's re-election launch and outlines priorities including housing, safety, community wellbeing, parks, arts and regional policing.

headline: Wendy Bowkett launches campaign for Victoria council
summary: Bowkett's campaign sets out positions on public accountability, community safety, non-market housing, parks and local economic planning.

headline: Melissa Cseszko enters Victoria council race
summary: Cseszko's campaign focuses on downtown conditions, business vitality, municipal accountability and protection of Victoria's heritage character.

headline: David Arthur Johnston
summary: Street Stories published a background profile of David Johnston covering his public presence, authorship of The Right to Sleep, involvement in camping-bylaw litigation and broader views. It is background coverage, not proof of a 2026 campaign position.

headline: Matt Dell confirms council re-election campaign
summary: Dell's campaign site confirms his re-election bid and sets out priorities on homes, a downtown library, parks, infrastructure, arts and local business.

headline: Jeremy Caradonna announces plans to seek re-election
summary: The report confirms Caradonna's re-election plans and says his developing platform centres community safety, sustainable urbanism, affordable housing and community infrastructure.
